items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: ‘Game, Set and Match’ is a tribute to Billie Jean King and Martina Navratilova

ctx.x: It has to do with music and meaning and intent. That your albums seem to have an intent, sometimes more obvious than others. And I was listening and reading about your “Portraits of Women in Motion.” I have a little quote — this was a review, I think you’re probably familiar with it. And the reviewer said, “For one thing Rowe’s writing is trying to tell a story and if you don’t know that ‘Game, Set and Match’ is a tribute to Billie Jean King and Martina Navratilova then the bouncing two note horn shots at the…

Yeah. So I will say that is one of the most overt attempts that I’ve ever made in any kind of music so yeah it was one of those things where I was really struggling to think how — because I don’t normally do this. I thought you know wouldn’t it be fun to see if I could. I played tennis all through high school and tried to play in college until I realized that Eastman School of Music did not have a tennis team and they did not want me running over to the University of Rochester. So you know I knew a lot about it…
